verdict.rationale: Vercel's Limits page documents per-plan wall-clock maximum function duration: Hobby 300s, Pro/Enterprise 300s default and 800s max, with up to 1800s in beta. It also documents per-plan vCPU/memory allocation, and the pricing page explains that Active CPU time is billed only during execution, not during I/O waits. The evidence does not state a distinct CPU-time execution cap, so the CPU half of the story covers resource allocation rather than a time limit. missing for 10: an explicit CPU-time limit for functions, guidance on fitting long-running or agentic workloads beyond the duration cap, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the limits.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I know the CPU and wall-clock execution time limits for functions so I can tell whether long-running or agentic workloads will fit

citations.quote: Maximum duration: 300s (5 minutes) default and max [Hobby] / 300s default, 800s max, up to 1800s (30 minutes) in beta [Pro and Enterprise]
Memory and CPU: 2 GB / 1 vCPU default and max [Hobby] / 2 GB / 1 vCPU default, up to 4 GB / 2 vCPU max [Pro and Enterprise]
This is the CPU time your code actively consumes in milliseconds. You are only billed during actual code execution and not during I/O operations
